<reflection>
After three experiments, M7 remains the best fit, but a group of mechanisms (M16, M11, M14, M20, M18, M17, M12) are within ~0.5 NLL units, indicating they are still plausible. Another cluster (M2, M13, M10, M15, M1) is about 0.7 NLL worse, but still competitive. The previous experiments varied catalyst concentration and added product, but substrate concentration has been constant at 1.0 M. To further discriminate among the mechanisms, varying substrate is a logical next step, as it will affect substrate-binding steps, potential substrate inhibition, and deactivation pathways that depend on substrate concentration.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Proposing an experiment with higher substrate concentration (2.0 M), low catalyst (0.01 M), and no initial product. This condition will probe the effect of substrate concentration on kinetics, which is expected to differentiate mechanisms with substrate-dependent steps. For example, M7 involves a second substrate binding to form catS2, which may show saturation or inhibition at high [S]. Mechanisms with substrate-induced deactivation (M11, M16) may exhibit stronger deactivation at higher [S]. In contrast, simple Michaelis-Menten type mechanisms (M1, M2) should show a more predictable saturation curve. By comparing this run with run 1 (S=1.0, cat=0.01, P=0), we can isolate the substrate effect while keeping catalyst constant, providing information that complements previous variations and helps spread NLL values across multiple candidate mechanisms simultaneously.
</hypothesis>
